parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations using the baseline controls should have less than 499 employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should list which parts of their information systems and assets are in scope for their implementation of the baseline controls and should provide the rationale for excluding information systems and assets and recognize the acceptance of risk in doing so.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should assess the potential injury to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability to their information systems and assets.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should self-identify their primary cyber threat.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should have a basic plan for how to respond to incidents of varying severity. If an organization is unable to manage some types of incidents on its own, the organization should have a plan for what it will do.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should have a written incident response plan that details who is responsible for handling incidents, including any relevant contact information for communicating to external parties, stakeholders, and regulators. Organizations should have an up-to-date hard copy version of this plan available for situations where soft copies are not available.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should consider purchasing a cyber security insurance policy that includes coverage for incident response and recovery activities OR provide a rationale for not purchasing one.

groups.title: Develop an Incident Response Plan (Elaborer un plan d intervention en cas d incident)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should enable automatic patching for all software and hardware OR establish full vulnerability and patch management solutions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should conduct risk assessment activities as to whether to replace any software and hardware that are not capable of automatic updates. If the organization chooses to keep such devices, they should have a business process to ensure regular manual updates.

groups.title: Automatically Patch Operating Systems and Applications (Appliquer automatiquement les correctifs)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should enable anti-malware solutions that update and scan automatically.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should activate any software firewalls included on the devices that are within organizational networks OR document the alternative measures in place instead of these firewalls.

groups.title: Enable Security Software (Activer les logiciels de securite)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should implement secure configurations for all their devices, changing all default passwords, turning off unnecessary features, and enabling all relevant security features.

groups.title: Securely Configure Devices (Configurer les appareils de facon securitaire)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should implement two-factor authentication wherever possible, and document all instances where they make the business decision not to do so. Organizations should require two-factor authentication for important accounts such as financial accounts, system administrators, cloud administration, privileged users, and senior executives.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should only enforce password changes on suspicion or evidence of compromise.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should have clear policies on password length and reuse, the use of password managers and if, when, and how users can physically write down and securely store a password.

groups.title: Strong User Authentication (Authentification forte des utilisateurs)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should invest in cyber security awareness and training for their employees.

groups.title: Employee Awareness Training (Sensibilisation et formation des employes)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should back up systems that contain essential business information, and ensure that recovery mechanisms effectively and efficiently restore these systems from back-ups. Organizations should consider storing back-ups offline at a secure offsite location OR provide the rationale for not doing so.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should securely store back-ups in an encrypted state, and restrict access to them to those who must access them for the testing or use of restoration activities. Long term backups (e.g. weekly backups) must be stored offline, but frequent backups (e.g. daily backups) may be stored online.

groups.title: Backup and Encrypt Data (Sauvegarder et chiffrer les donnees)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should decide on an ownership model for mobile devices and document the rationale and associated risks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should enforce separation between work and personal data on mobile devices with access to corporate IT resources, and document the details of this separation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should ensure that employees only download mobile device apps from the organization’s list of trusted sources.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should require that all mobile devices store all sensitive information in a secure, encrypted state.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should consider implementing an enterprise mobility management solution for all mobile devices OR document the risks assumed to the audit, management, and security functionality of mobile devices by not implementing such a solution.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should enforce or educate users to (1) disable automatic connections to open networks, (2) avoid connecting to unknown Wi-Fi networks, (3) limit the use of Bluetooth and NFC for the exchange of sensitive information, and (4) use corporate Wi-Fi or cellular data network connectivity rather than public Wi-Fi.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should consider using a VPN if they require connectivity to public Wi-Fi networks OR provide the rationale for not using a VPN.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should have dedicated firewalls at the boundaries between its corporate network and the Internet. The organization should isolate Internet-facing servers from the rest of their corporate network.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should implement a DNS firewall for outbound DNS requests to the Internet.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should require secure connectivity to all corporate IT resources, and require VPN connectivity with two-factor authentication for all remote access into corporate networks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should only use secure Wi-Fi, preferably WPA2-Enterprise.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should never connect public Wi-Fi networks to their corporate networks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should isolate point-of-sale systems from the Internet and other areas of the corporate network with a firewall. Organizations should consider following the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should ensure the implementation of DMARC on all of the organization’s email services.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should implement email filtering at points of ingress and egress.

groups.title: Establish Basic Perimeter Defences (Etablir des defenses de perimetre de base)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should require that all their cloud service providers share an AICPA SSAE 18 SOC 3 report that states that they achieved Trust Service Principles compliance.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should evaluate their comfort level with how their outsourced IT providers handle and access their sensitive information.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should evaluate their comfort level with the legal jurisdictions where their outsourced providers store or use their sensitive information.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should ensure that their IT infrastructure and users communicate securely with all cloud services and applications.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should ensure that administrative accounts for cloud services use two-factor authentication and differ from internal administrator accounts.

groups.title: Secure Cloud and Outsourced IT Services (Securiser les services infonuagiques et TI impartis)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should ensure that their websites address the OWASP top 10 vulnerabilities.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should ensure that they understand the ASVS level they need to meet for each of their websites.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should provision accounts with the minimum functionality necessary for tasks and in particular should restrict administrator privileges to an as-required basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should only permit administrator accounts to perform administrative activities (and not user-level activities such as accessing email or browsing the web).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should remove accounts and/or functionality when employees no longer require these for their tasks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should consider implementing a centralized authorization control system OR provide a rationale for not implementing a centralized authorization control system.

groups.title: Implement Access Control and Authorization (Mettre en oeuvre le controle d acces)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should mandate the sole use of organization-owned secure portable media, have strong asset controls for these devices, and require the use of encryption on all of these devices.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizations should have processes for the sanitization or destruction of portable media prior to disposal.

groups.title: Secure Portable Media (Securiser les supports amovibles)

metadata.remarks: National cyber security standard CAN/DGSI 104 and CCCS Baseline Cyber Security Controls for Small and Medium Organizations administered by the Standards Council of Canada (SCC) and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.
metadata.title: CyberSecure Canada - Baseline Cyber Security Controls for Small and Medium Organizations
